headline: Last session: Indian benchmarks post longest weekly losing run in 25 years as Sensex crashes 1,000 points

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Tuesday, 6 October.

why: Massive en-masse selling of Indian stocks by foreign institutional investors
Global risks and geopolitical tensions, including potential closure of the Strait of Hormuz
Equity markets experiencing an eight-week decline, the longest in 25 years
Significant wealth erosion with ₹9 lakh crore wiped out in a single session
whatHappening: DLF successfully sold all 172 senior living homes in its Gurugram project for ₹1,985 crore
FSSAI recalled Everest Cumin Powder and suspended Creative Bakers' license over safety concerns
Flipkart doubled its active seller base to enhance its ecommerce platform presence
Analysts predict continued market volatility for the upcoming trading week starting Tuesday
summary: The Indian stock market is closed for the weekend after benchmarks recorded their longest weekly losing streak in 25 years. Driven by heavy FII selling and global risks, the Sensex recently crashed 1,000 points, though DLF reported strong sales for its Gurugram project. Investors are now looking toward Tuesday's reopening for signs of recovery amidst ongoing volatility.
